Looking at the regex pattern: `r"\\?</?((?:[fb]g\s)?[^<>\s]*)>"`

This pattern matches:
- Optionally a backslash `\\?`
- Then `<` 
- Optionally `/` for closing tags
- Then the tag name part
- Then `>`

So when we have `r"\\<le>test</le>"`, the regex will match:
1. `\\<le>` - the first tag with a leading backslash
2. `</le>` - the closing tag

The problem is in the logic at line 230-232:
```python
if markup[0] == "\\":
    self._tokens.append((TokenType.TEXT, markup[1:]))
    continue
```

When it encounters `\\<le>`, it strips the first backslash and treats `<le>` as literal text (which is correct).

But then it encounters `</le>` and tries to parse it as a closing tag. Since there was no opening `<le>` tag (it was escaped), it raises the error.

The issue is that when we have `\\<le>`, we should treat BOTH backslashes as escaping characters, meaning the entire sequence `<le>` should be treated as literal text, not as an opening tag. 

However, the current regex and logic only considers the first backslash as the escape character, leaving the `<le>` part to be parsed normally.

So when we have `r"\\<le>test</le>"`, the parsing should be:
- `\\<le>` -> literal text `<le>` (both backslashes escape the tag)
- `test` -> literal text  
- `</le>` -> literal text (since there was no opening tag)

But currently it's:
- `\\<le>` -> literal text `<le>` (first backslash escapes, `<le>` becomes literal)  
- `test` -> literal text
- `</le>` -> tries to parse as closing tag -> ERROR because no opening tag

The fix needs to properly handle the case where multiple backslashes are used for escaping.
